topic.title: Knowledge Transfer, Teaching, and Distillation
topic.overview: Knowledge distillation trains one model using information supplied by another, but a more accurate teacher is not automatically a more useful teacher. The topic includes student-friendly representations, transfer between heterogeneous architectures, self-distillation, and retaining existing skills while incorporating new knowledge. A smaller educational strand studies how latent skills and teaching examples support learning.
topic.whyItMatters: Transfer quality depends on what the learner can represent and which signals the teacher exposes. Compression or adaptation can remove noise, but may also erase information needed for later tasks.
topic.evolution: The representatives include educational skill discovery and machine teaching before and alongside modern neural distillation. Recent papers analyze whether distillation transfers the intended behavior and use context-conditioned teachers for continual language-model adaptation. This grouping connects learning from other learners, not a demonstrated historical dependency between tutoring models and neural compression.
openQuestions: How can teacher signals be matched to a student’s representational limits?
When does self-distillation denoise knowledge rather than progressively forget useful distinctions?
